summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with a history of inoperable cholangiocarcinoma and recurrent biliary infections, was admitted for fever (101.2°F) and blood from his percutaneous biliary drain (PTBD). Initial evaluation revealed stable vital signs, mild lab abnormalities, and two new hypodense liver lesions on CT, concerning for microabscesses. Blood cultures were negative, but catheter tip cultures grew gram-negative rods and Enterococcus. He underwent successful exchange of his PTBD catheter, with cholangiogram confirming patent ducts and no obstruction. He was treated with IV meropenem, then transitioned to a four-week course of outpatient ertapenem as recommended by infectious disease. His symptoms improved, delirium resolved, and he was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotics. Follow-up was arranged with oncology, infectious disease, and primary care to monitor response and consider repeat imaging.
